meta.title: Magic state cultivation on Willow

paper.authors: E. Rosenfeld, G. Roberts, N. Lacroix, A. Bourassa et al. (Google Quantum AI)
paper.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor

meta.summary: A |T⟩ state injected into a distance-3 color code, checked twice by measuring the logical Hadamard (T·X·T†) with postselection, and grafted into a distance-5 code on 54 transmons: about 40 times less error than injection alone.
meta.program: Two levels. The factory is the paper's own circuit, qubit for qubit: the supplement links every circuit it ran as a Crumble URL (copied verbatim into this repository), whose tagged identities name the T gates, echoes and injection angle the hardware played. The call is a FormalRV program that consumes one magic state (`prepare |T>`: the `request_magic` system call, a Z⊗Z merge, an X readout, a frame update) on a distance-5 surface-code block, compiled against a machine whose factory is that circuit on the twin.
meta.twin: The transmons each circuit uses, at the circuit's own grid coordinates, a coupler between every pair one lattice step apart, 35 ns single-qubit and CZ gates (the paper's supplement), readout and reset from the group's 2023 paper. One RISC-Q core per transmon at 500 MHz; a T gate is a 45° pulse (half the 90° amplitude, same 35 ns), an echo an X pulse, a Hadamard a 90° pulse with a virtual Z.
findings: The circuits are the paper's: the kickback circuit has the 216 two-qubit gates and 54 measurements the text states, the grafting circuit the 54 qubits, and every CZ of all three lies on a coupler between grid neighbours. Run noiselessly with its real T gates (45° pulses), the kickback circuit keeps |T⟩ with no detector firing and rejects the orthogonal state every time.

On the twin every operation of all three circuits ran inside its window: cultivation with standard tomography takes 3.62 µs, kickback tomography 14.05 µs (1308 pulses), injection, cultivation and graft on 54 transmons 7.24 µs. The controller's 2 ns grid turns the paper's 35 ns layers into 36 ns.

Control needs one RISC-Q core per transmon. A core issues a timed write in 35 to 63 of its cycles (measured on the core model that matches RISC-Q's RTL), 70 to 126 ns at 500 MHz, so back-to-back 36 ns layers are kept only because the core gets ahead into its 32-entry queue; with two transmons per core the firmware generator refuses the kickback circuit (one channel would have to be 33 writes ahead). A measured bit reaches its core's memory 64 ns after the readout window; the paper postselects offline, so no gate waits for it. One ZCU216 holds at most 14 RISC-Q cores, so the 54-qubit graft (56 cores) needs at least 4 boards; the Lean run keeps them on one board, so bits that would cross boards are not delayed (about 0.6 µs a crossing on RISC-Q's board-to-board network).

Under the paper's own noise model (SI1000, p = 2.3×10⁻³) the kickback circuit keeps 11.9% of shots, against the 8% of the experiment, with 2.1×10⁻⁵ error among kept shots (75 flips in 3.6 million), below the experiment's 1–2×10⁻⁴. Between p = 1.5×10⁻³ and 4×10⁻³ the error grows as p^3.4, close to the p³ of fault distance three (Supplementary Fig. S19).

As a system call: FormalRV compiled a T gate on a distance-5 surface-code block against a machine whose factory is the 54-qubit graft circuit (25 output and 29 workspace qubits, 7.244 µs), and its VM admitted the listing (RESOURCE_VALIDATED). The factory's 54 qubits plus the program's block fit Willow's 105.

FormalRV's factory contract has a fixed latency and no acceptance probability. Cultivation keeps 62.8% of its attempts here (the Fig. 2 circuit), so a kept state takes 11.5 µs on average, 1.6 times what FormalRV reserves; a call to `request_magic` is a repeat-until-success service.
limits: The noise numbers come from the Clifford proxy the paper's own Stim circuits define (T gates as tagged identities, |+⟩ injected): the paper compares experiment with state-vector simulation, which is not repeated here. The state-vector run with the real T gates is noiseless (it checks the circuit, not the noise).
Readout (500 ns) and reset (160 ns) are the group's 2023 values; the cultivation paper gives neither, so the circuits' times on the twin rest on them.
An `I[conjugate]` pulse is taken as an X pulse: the paper says it restores the Pauli frame before a T layer but its Stim circuit does not say which Pauli.
The grafted code of Fig. 4 is decoded in the paper with Tesseract; its noise is not simulated here, and the factory's acceptance is that of the Fig. 2 circuit (injection and cultivation).

Only the transmons a circuit uses are placed: the full coordinate map of the 105-qubit chip is not published. Pulse shapes and frequencies are RISC-Q's x6y3 calibration at the paper's durations; leakage, crosstalk and flux transients are not modeled.

device.basis: The circuit is the paper's own (Supplementary "Explicit circuits", Crumble links), qubit for qubit. Gate durations are the paper's; readout and reset are not given there and come from the group's 2023 surface-code paper. Every CZ of the circuit must be on a coupler of the square grid (checked). Pulse shapes, frequencies and the readout multiplexing are not published: the chip reuses RISC-Q's x6y3 calibration shapes at these durations. The controller is QuantumOS's RISC-Q model, not Google's.

verdictDetail.scope: Resource admission for the printed schedule: physical register bounds, compositional allocation/release identities, exclusive qubit use, machine capacities, and gadget/program upper budgets. Factory internals are the authored service contract. Conservative loop/call envelopes and all-taken guards. Does not certify quantum semantics, classical record causality/SSA, declarative protocol interfaces, lower bounds, or optimality.

protocol_findings.scope: Report only: rules this VM does not enforce; nothing here refuses and no other field depends on it. count: record bits, or gate executions; first_line: the least line of a counted finding. first: the first item of that line, null at count 0: line, unit (the gadget holding the line, or program), statement (the listing line without its time stamp, at most 240 bytes), callee (when the statement is a call); register, address, bits (the first offending cells in the listing's operand syntax reg[lo:hi], as the frame that counts them holds them: numbers at program scope, a loop's binder and a gadget's formals inside a body; for a gate its operands and qubits); operand (the statement's own clause that names the cells, as written); via (for cells of a statement inside a gadget that are counted at program scope: the program statement they came through, with its callee); port (for cells of a call's or loop's port: the whole port); inside (another statement the cells originate at, when the VM keeps it). bound exact: the program has no loop, guard, case or call and was compared cell by cell. gate_without_route (C4's rule of the staged compiler, on each frame's own statements): a two-qubit gate with no route statement of its frame that holds every operand, is complete by the gate's start and was not ended by a later route, allocation or release of one of its qubits or by a child that uses one; a frame's count times its calls and trips, guards as taken, the larger of alternatives; bound upper for this rule (a containment not shown counts); the compiler's local-rounds exemption is not applied. read_unwritten: cells a statement reads for which no write complete by the read is found among the other statements and children of its frame, nor of any enclosing frame up to the program; a loop's reads leave as the hull over its trips unless an earlier trip writes them. read_before_decode: the same for a value read (parity, frame update, guard) and a decode or a parity's output. Both bound upper under two conventions of this VM: a producer under a guard or in a case arm counts as run, and a producer port that is a hull (a loop whose trips leave gaps, a group of more than 4096 pieces) counts for all its cells; a cell written again keeps an earlier decode's credit. syndrome_never_decoded: cells of a syndrome write for which no decode input whose read is not before the write's completion is found among the other statements and children of its frame, nor of any enclosing frame up to the program (a loop's pending writes leave as the hull over its trips unless a later trip decodes them); bound upper under the same two conventions, a decode in place of a producer; a cell decoded and written again is counted. syndrome_bits_written, syndrome_bits_decoded: the syndrome bits that statements write and that decodes read, per execution (guards as taken, the larger of alternatives). record_overwrite: record bits outside source registers written by two statements or children of one frame (same address shape), or again by a later trip of a loop (stride below width), summed over walked frames times calls and trips (bound frame_sum: not a bound). record_rewritten_before_read: record bits (of source registers too) that are read (a value read or a decode's input) after something written LATER in the program has written the same cells again, so that the read sees that value and not the one the program had written before it. In a frame: the read's cells that a write (for a value read also a decode) of a later statement or child holds, of the same address shape and issued by the read's last time (the refusing checks make it complete by the first); not the cells that a statement before the reader produces in full after that producer is complete. In a loop whose trips have a period: per read port of the body the bits that later trips' write ports of the same address shape and stride have written again by the read's first time, over the trips that have such a later trip. Summed over walked frames times calls and trips (bound frame_sum: a child's port is a hull of cells with one time window, a child's read port counts its cells once whatever the number of reads behind it, and a guard counts as taken; writes and decodes are compared apart, so a later owner's write is not hidden by an earlier owner's decode that completes after it. Cells of different address shapes are not compared: pairs_not_compared counts the pairs of a read and a group of producers of another shape that the bounds do not show apart, in every frame walked, and above 0 the count may miss reads. By default the count is a rule (RECORD_REWRITTEN; --no-record-order only counts) and those pairs are decided: under an obligation checked where a gadget's formals are numbers, or by cutting the loops whose indices tell the shapes apart). would_refuse_require_specs: the first refusal the checks of --require-specs reach in this run, or null. comment_lines: lines of the listing holding #. untracked_ports above 0: record ports dropped where a site could not be moved or compared; the record counts may then miss reads. Null counts: the walk did not complete, or --bounds-only.
